source.title: Retinotopic coding organizes the interaction between internally and externally oriented brain networks

confidence_rationale: Citation verified exact, including the 2026-09-08 revision date, and the reported result matches the claim note almost word for word. Held near 0.5 by preprint status (not a version of record), by the small-N densely-sampled design, and because retinotopy is one specific sensory coordinate while MECH-555 is a general claim about relational indexing.
failure_signatures: Coupling organised by shared visual-field preference is correlational resting-state structure; no manipulation permutes the frame while holding content fixed, which is exactly the discriminator MECH-555 requires.

The interactions are bivalent (negative-amplitude DN voxels anticorrelate with matched dATN voxels, positive-amplitude ones correlate), so 'shared frame implies coupling' is too simple a reading of this result.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Using densely sampled 7T fMRI with individualised parcellations and voxel-wise population-receptive- field mapping, spontaneous coupling between the Default Network and the dorsal attention network is shaped by the latent visual-field preferences of individual voxels, even though the two networks are uncorrelated at the whole-network level. Retinotopic coding is intrinsic to the DN and persists during elevated top-down drive.
mapping.ree_translation: An existence proof that two systems which are globally distinct can nonetheless have their interaction organised by a shared indexing coordinate -- the biological motivation for treating reference frame as a separable interface factor alongside content and communication subspace.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Adopted verbatim from MECH-555's own caution: retinotopy is NOT to be copied into REE, no universal coordinate vocabulary is prescribed, and a shared indexing relation across several consumers must not be read as evidence for one global workspace or one shared object. This is a reviewed preprint, not a version of record, and per feedback_lit_exp_decoupled it raises no claim's confidence.
mapping.source_context: Human 7T fMRI, resting state plus independent retinotopic mapping; dense sampling of few individuals.

confidence_components.notes: Dense-sampling 7T with individualised network definitions is methodologically strong per subject and weak in population generality. Preprint status is the other discount.
